brief:
Since leaving Gaza, displaced Palestinians report that everyday life and major events alike have become emotionally hollow, according to We Are Not Numbers. Former residents describe an existence fundamentally altered by separation from home, where even significant occasions no longer bring satisfaction or joy.

The accounts reflect a pattern among Gaza's diaspora: material circumstances of exile do not restore a sense of purpose. Displaced Palestinians say that the routines and milestones that once carried weight now feel devoid of vitality, suggesting separation from home inflicts damage beyond physical displacement or economic hardship.
dek: Since leaving Gaza, everything has lost its sparkle, from the smallest routine to the grandest occasion.
title: Gazans displaced abroad describe life stripped of meaning and joy
